## Spoken end cards and gallery episode automation

Every vertical short for social media gets burned-in captions from measured word timing, with one of six style presets. Caption style, opening order, and code-card theme rotate across a series so the videos do not share one structure. Install walkthroughs are opt-in.

Vertical shorts open on an integration poster before any footage; a gallery integration episode opens on its hook footage and keeps the cover as the thumbnail.

Gallery episodes now end with the catalog's closing line spoken over the end card, the one spoken call to action in any video: "To try this integration, go to the py-shinywidgets website." The narration pauses before the line; the card appears on its first words and stays to the end. `reel.yaml` accepts `outro.spoken` to name the phrase, `stitch_reel.py` renders the card as the last shot instead of a silent tail, and `burn_captions.py --stop-at` stops the burned-in captions before the line so they never double the card's text.

The integration episode starter ships verified browser-capture tooling for the tested Lonboard episode. `capture.yaml` records the setup, the per-orientation pixel points, and each action with the phrase it lands on. `capture.py` preflights every action and prints the real values for the narration, then records each action against the measured narration; a clip that opens on a box gets its first corner pressed off camera. `assemble.py` places the recorded clips around the code still and renders the spoken end card, replacing `interaction-shot.yaml`. While the catalog says `released: false`, install shinywidgets from the repository and keep the install command off the end card.

Supporting changes: captions keep zero-duration words such as "a", the bootstrap script reads the variant from the production lock for `--local` snapshots, and the Claude skill is back under its compactness limit.

Both skill variants ship the new tooling and the updated guidance. New productions automatically verify and pin this release. Existing productions keep their current snapshot.
